buildings.name: Keep
buildings.description: The heart of your kingdom. Its level sets how much of every good you can keep, and raising it unlocks new buildings and higher levels. Destroying it wins a star.

buildings.name: House
buildings.description: Home to a villager. Every villager builds, upgrades or clears one thing at a time.

buildings.name: Farm
buildings.description: Fields of wheat that feed your people and your army. Farms side by side help each other.

buildings.name: Sawmill
buildings.description: Woodcutters work the forest, which never runs out. Every tree and grove within reach makes it faster.

buildings.name: Quarry
buildings.description: Masons cut and dress stone for walls, towers and keeps. The quarry never runs dry.

buildings.name: Mine
buildings.description: Miners dig ore from deep shafts and smelt it into iron for armour, siege engines and cannons. The seam never runs out.

buildings.name: Granary
buildings.description: A strongroom for your food. Raiders can reach only what the vaults hold — the higher it stands, the less they carry off.

buildings.name: Storehouse
buildings.description: A strongroom for timber, stone and iron. The higher it stands, the less raiders carry off.

buildings.name: Market
buildings.description: Merchants buy and sell food, wood, stone and iron for gold at the world price. A bigger market takes a smaller cut.

buildings.name: Barracks
buildings.description: The infantry school: swordsmen, archers, pillagers, breachers, crossbowmen, monks, shieldbearers and firebrands. Its level sets how many soldiers train side by side.

buildings.name: Stable
buildings.description: Horses and riders: knights, scouts and — for the mightiest lords — elephants.

buildings.name: Workshop
buildings.description: Carpenters build Rams, and Trebuchets at level 2. Its level also sets how many siege engines an army may bring: 1, then 2.

buildings.name: Camp
buildings.description: Your trained troops wait here, ready to march.

buildings.name: Academy
buildings.description: Scholars and smiths study your troops here, making them stronger.

buildings.name: Cannon
buildings.description: A heavy bombard. Strong shots at one ground target at a time.
buildings.aiming: It keeps on one raider until he falls, and never wastes a shot on one already done for.

buildings.name: Tower
buildings.description: Archers on a tall tower. Long range and quick to fire.
buildings.aiming: It keeps on one raider until he falls, and never wastes a shot on one already done for.

buildings.name: Mortar
buildings.description: Lobs heavy shells that burst on landing, crushing groups of troops. Cannot hit anything too close.
buildings.aiming: It lobs each shell where the thickest crowd will be when it lands, never inside its minimum range.

buildings.name: Bastion
buildings.description: A stone keep bristling with archers. Fires volleys at three targets at once and takes a beating.
buildings.aiming: It spreads each volley over different raiders.

buildings.name: Ballista
buildings.description: A great bolt-thrower. Its iron bolts fly straight through every raider in their path, and hit riders and siege engines hardest.
buildings.aiming: It aims each bolt down the line that runs through the most raiders.

buildings.name: Wall
buildings.description: Keeps raiders out — they must break through or walk around. Starts as a wooden palisade.

buildings.name: Keg
buildings.description: A hidden keg of blasting powder. Bursts when raiders walk close.

buildings.name: Hall
buildings.description: The great hall where your heroes live: the Lord from level 1, the Lady from level 3. Its level sets how far they can train, and while they are at home and rested they guard it from raiders.

buildings.name: Armoury
buildings.description: Quartermasters ready one-use battle tactics: War Horns, Herbs (level 1) and Smoke Pots (level 2). Each level holds one more, and makes them stronger.

buildings.name: Pit
buildings.description: A hidden pit full of stakes. Swallows the first raider who treads on it — a siege engine, whole.

buildings.name: Caltrops
buildings.description: Iron spikes scattered in the grass. Once raiders find them, everyone crossing the patch limps along at half speed, bleeding.

buildings.name: Tar Pit
buildings.description: A sunken trough of pitch. Raiders who wade in set it off: a moment later it bursts into flame and burns everyone around.

buildings.name: Snare
buildings.description: A noose of rope hidden in the grass, for riders only: it holds a horse fast for a few seconds while the defences do the rest.

buildings.name: Ambush
buildings.description: Archers hidden in a dugout. When raiders come close they leap out and fight to the last.

targetModes.label: Nearest
targetModes.hint: Whoever comes closest, until he falls

targetModes.label: Riders first
targetModes.hint: Pillagers, scouts, knights and elephants before anyone else

targetModes.label: Siege first
targetModes.hint: Rams, breachers and trebuchets before anyone else

targetModes.label: Finish them
targetModes.hint: Monks first, then the raider with the least health left

troops.name: Swordsman
troops.description: Mail, sword and shield. Cheap, steady and quick to train — the backbone of every army.

troops.name: Archer
troops.description: A longbow that reaches over walls. Fragile up close — keep archers behind the front line.

troops.name: Pillager
troops.description: A fast rider with a torch who goes straight for granaries, storehouses and the Keep's stores, and strikes them twice as hard.

troops.name: Knight
troops.description: Plate armour on a barded warhorse. Charges the defences and soaks up a great deal of punishment.

troops.name: Ram
troops.description: A roofed timber ram that only attacks buildings. Smashes walls in a few blows, and arrows barely scratch it.

troops.name: Trebuchet
troops.description: A great counterweight engine that hurls boulders at the nearest building from beyond the defences' reach. Slow, can't hit anything closer than three tiles, and takes one of the army's siege slots.

troops.name: Crossbowman
troops.description: A heavy crossbow whose bolts punch through timber and stone: goes for the defences and hits them half again as hard. Slow to reload.

troops.name: Breacher
troops.description: Runs at the nearest wall with a keg of blasting powder and blows a hole in it — and in himself.

troops.name: Monk
troops.description: Walks with the biggest group of soldiers and heals the wounded around him. A soldier tended by several monks heals little faster; monks heal each other but never themselves, machines can't be healed, heroes and elephants heal slowly.

troops.name: Elephant
troops.description: A mountain in armour. Slow, but it tramples everything around its target and shrugs off arrows.

troops.name: Scout
troops.description: A light rider sent ahead of the army. Lifts the mist around him, never springs a trap, marks and disarms the hidden ones he finds, and rides up to the defences to show how far they reach. Two at most in an army.

troops.name: Shieldbearer
troops.description: Carries a great painted pavise at the defences. Every soldier close behind him takes 30% less from arrows, bolts and cannonballs.

troops.name: Firebrand
troops.description: Looses burning arrows over the walls. Whatever he hits catches fire and keeps burning for a while.

lord.name: Lord
lord.description: You, at the head of your army, on a white charger. Rides for the defences, takes a great deal of punishment, and once ashore can sound Rally! — healing and hastening every soldier around him.

lady.name: Lady
lady.description: The Lady of the Keep, with a longbow taller than she is. Shoots over walls from afar, and once ashore can raise her Banner — the soldiers around her take much less damage for a while, and she looses three arrows a shot.

chapters.title: Smoke on the Shore
chapters.story: Raven sails were seen at dawn. By noon the fishing villages along our coast were burning. Red Hagga's raiders hold them now — take them back, Lord, one by one.

chapters.title: The Fenland Forts
chapters.story: Hagga fled inland to the fens, where the Bog Baron hides the Ravens' plunder behind reed walls and black water. His forts are cunning. So must we be.

chapters.title: The Iron Hills
chapters.story: Every blade the Ravens carry is forged in the Iron Hills. Brask Ironjaw works the furnaces day and night. Break his forges, and the Raven fleet goes to sea with blunt swords.

chapters.title: The Raven's Roost
chapters.story: At last the trail leads to the sea itself — to the Roost, the Raven King's fortress on the cliffs. Our longboats will carry the army ashore. Our people are with us. It ends where the land meets the sea.

chapters.title: The Imperial Age
chapters.story: With the Ravens gone, ships came from every port on the sea — and among them the grey sails of the Ashen Empire, whose gold paid for Corvane's war. Marshal Varro wants our coast for his emperor. Our kingdom is no longer a corner of the sea, Lord. Time to stand like an empire.

strongholds.name: Burnt Landing
strongholds.intro: The first village the Ravens took is still smoking. A handful of raiders and one stolen cannon hold it. Show them whose coast this is.
strongholds.hint: One stolen cannon, and it can only fire at one man at a time. Watch whom it picks — and whom it can't reach.
strongholds.outro: The villagers are coming home. Word of your victory will travel up the coast faster than any ship.

strongholds.name: Net Sheds
strongholds.intro: Past the burnt village, the Ravens have turned our net sheds into a lookout. One watch tower sees the whole beach, and its archers never miss a man in the open.
strongholds.hint: A watch tower reaches further than any archer of ours. Somebody must walk up under its arrows — who can take them best?
strongholds.outro: The lookout is down. Our nets will be dry by evening.

strongholds.name: Gull Rock Watch
strongholds.intro: A tower on Gull Rock signals the raiders whenever our boats put out. It stands high over the beach and sees everything that comes near.
strongholds.hint: That tower sees everything that comes near. Archers can't take many arrows; swordsmen can take a few. Whom would you rather it shot at?
strongholds.outro: The tower is dark. Our fishing boats can sail again.

strongholds.name: Fisher's Rest
strongholds.intro: Hagga's men have walled themselves in at Fisher's Rest. Your swordsmen alone would batter at that palisade all day.
strongholds.hint: A palisade laughs at swords. One thing in your company was built for walls; think about what it needs from the others.
strongholds.outro: A ram and a breach — the oldest trick in war, and still the best.

strongholds.name: Tide Mill
strongholds.intro: The raiders hold the tide mill behind a stockade with two gaps the tide washed out. They think nobody has noticed.
strongholds.hint: A wall is only as good as its worst stretch. Look along it before you start hacking.
strongholds.outro: In through the gaps and out with the flour. The miller will mend his stockade properly this time.

strongholds.name: Old Tollgate
strongholds.intro: The raiders took the old tollgate on the coast road. The gate stands wide open, as if they want us to walk in.
strongholds.hint: An open gate is an invitation, and Ravens don't invite guests out of kindness.
strongholds.outro: Not one of our men stepped on a keg. Hagga's tricks will need to get better.

strongholds.name: Cinder Mill
strongholds.intro: Cinder Mill feeds Hagga's army: farms and mills spread across the valley, and only a few guards inside the stockade.
strongholds.hint: The stockade is small and the fields are wide. Wide ground wants fast feet.
strongholds.outro: Without the mill's bread, Hagga's raiders will be hungry tonight.

strongholds.name: Smokehouse Row
strongholds.intro: Hagga keeps her smoked fish and stolen salt in a long walled row by the harbour. No ram could reach those walls across the open yard.
strongholds.hint: Some soldiers are worth one blow and no more. Spend that blow on the stone that matters.
strongholds.outro: The walls came down with a bang, and the salt is ours again.

strongholds.name: Lantern Point
strongholds.intro: On Lantern Point the Ravens have set up a mortar. Its shells fall slow and wide — one lands among a crowd, and the crowd is gone.
strongholds.hint: A mortar loves a crowd and can't hit what stands at its feet. Think about both.
strongholds.outro: The mortar is spiked and the lantern lit for our ships again.

strongholds.name: Saltmarsh Keep
strongholds.intro: Red Hagga herself waits in Saltmarsh Keep, behind two cannons and a tower. Take the keep and the coast is ours again.
strongholds.hint: Hagga's tower hunts siege engines before anything else. How do you get a ram to a wall it is watching?
strongholds.outro: Hagga escaped in a reed boat, cursing your name. She is running for the fens — and we will follow.

strongholds.name: Reedwall Gate
strongholds.intro: The fens begin at Reedwall. Two towers on the reed wall rain arrows on anything that moves, and the Baron's men love to watch.
strongholds.hint: Every arrow those towers loose is meant for soft men. Who in your company was made to stand in front of the others?
strongholds.outro: Reedwall has fallen. The Baron will hear of it by nightfall.

strongholds.name: Bog Causeway
strongholds.intro: A single causeway crosses the bog to the Baron's outpost. Its defenders fight from behind the palisade, and our swords are too short to reach them.
strongholds.hint: A sword can't reach over a palisade. An arrow can — and a palisade can be opened.
strongholds.outro: The causeway is ours. The archers are already arguing about who struck first.

strongholds.name: Duskwater Ford
strongholds.intro: Marsh fog lies thick on Duskwater Ford, and the Baron has seeded the shallows with pits, spikes and powder. Three of our crews went into that fog and never came out.
strongholds.hint: In this fog you won't see the Baron's surprises until somebody steps on them. Better that somebody is quick, light, and looking.
strongholds.outro: The ford is ours. The scouts have marked every trap the Baron left — and kept a few for themselves.

strongholds.name: Eel Weirs
strongholds.intro: The Baron guards his eel weirs with ballistas — great crossbows whose bolts go clean through one man and into the next.
strongholds.hint: A ballista bolt flies straight and doesn't stop at the first man. A column is a gift to it.
strongholds.outro: The weirs are ours, and the eels are for our cooks.

strongholds.name: Twin Moats
strongholds.intro: The Baron rings his treasure house with wall after wall of black oak. Hack at them and you will still be hacking at nightfall.
strongholds.hint: Wall behind wall: the Baron is counting on you wearing yourself out before the middle. Must every wall be broken, or only the right ones?
strongholds.outro: Two walls, two breaches, one very surprised Baron's steward.

strongholds.name: Mossy Abbey
strongholds.intro: The Baron turned the old abbey into a fort and set two cannons in its cloister. A slow charge across that yard would be cut to pieces.
strongholds.hint: Those cannons will grind down any slow charge. A cannon can face only one way at a time — give them more than one thing to look at.
strongholds.outro: The monks of the abbey have their home back. They have promised to march with us — and to pray for us. Loudly.

strongholds.name: Peat Cutters
strongholds.intro: The peat cutters' camp is ringed with guns and towers, each one covering the next. A frontal charge would never reach them.
strongholds.hint: Some bolts were made to crack stone and timber. Keep the men who loose them alive, and the guns will fall one by one.
strongholds.outro: The guns are silent, and the peat will warm our people this winter instead of the Baron's.

strongholds.name: Thornback Hold
strongholds.intro: Thornback is built all of black oak: a palisade no axe can bite, and behind it a ballista, towers, stores and stables of the same timber.
strongholds.hint: Black oak turns a sword, and everything behind that palisade is timber too. Some fights are better started from outside — and left to finish themselves.
strongholds.outro: Thornback burned all night. The fens are opening up before us.

strongholds.name: Heron Watch
strongholds.intro: Heron Watch guards the last road to the Baron's hall: a fort of black oak in the fog, a mortar in its yard and pits in the reeds around it.
strongholds.hint: Everything you learned in the fens, in one fort. Use your tools in the order the fort asks for them.
strongholds.outro: The watch has fallen. Through the fog we can see the Baron's hall at last.

strongholds.name: Fenmoor Hall
strongholds.intro: Baron Fenmoor's own hall rises out of the marsh fog: a mortar on the roof, a ballista at the gate, walls of black oak — and the ground around it worked with traps.
strongholds.hint: The Baron has an answer for every trick you learned in the fens. Has he an answer for all of them at once?
strongholds.outro: The Baron surrendered and told us everything: the Ravens' swords come from the Iron Hills.

strongholds.name: Copperhill
strongholds.intro: The first forge-town of the Iron Hills. Brask's gunners stand shoulder to shoulder on the ridge, every gun covering the next.
strongholds.hint: Brask packed most of his guns close so each can guard the others; one tower watches from the side. A stone that lands among them doesn't have to choose.
strongholds.outro: Copperhill's furnaces are cold. Brask Ironjaw will feel the draught.

strongholds.name: Slag Heaps
strongholds.intro: Between the slag heaps Brask has dug in his guns. Our foot soldiers would be cut down long before they reached them — but armour on horseback is another matter.
strongholds.hint: Heavy riders go straight for the guns and shrug off arrows. Let them draw the fire, and let the rest follow.
strongholds.outro: The knights rode through the guns as if they were made of straw. Brask will hear the hoofbeats in his sleep.

strongholds.name: Grimstone Quarry
strongholds.intro: At Grimstone the cannons sit inside the quarry's stone walls — and the quarrymen have been digging outside them, too.
strongholds.hint: Quarrymen dig more than stone. The ground in front of those walls has been worked, and it is hungry for something heavy.
strongholds.outro: The quarry is ours — and the stone is better than the Ravens deserved.

strongholds.name: Bellows Yard
strongholds.intro: The bellows yard is Brask's barracks: a Bastion full of swordsmen and archers who march out the moment anyone comes near.
strongholds.hint: Come within reach of the Bastion and its garrison comes out to meet you. Decide where that meeting happens.
strongholds.outro: The garrison lies beaten in its own yard. The bellows have stopped breathing.

strongholds.name: Ember Gorge
strongholds.intro: Brask's furnaces in Ember Gorge sit behind three rings of stone, and ballistas on the gorge's rim hunt every engine that comes near.
strongholds.hint: Three rings of stone you need not cross — if your engines live long enough to throw. What can't be seen can't be aimed at.
strongholds.outro: The gorge glows no more. Every stone the trebuchets threw was one less blade for the Ravens.

strongholds.name: Wolfpine Lodge
strongholds.intro: Brask's hunting lodge sits deep in the pines, its towers and guns scattered among the trees — and his huntsmen's snares in every glade.
strongholds.hint: A man caught in a noose is a target that can't run. Something has to walk those glades before the company does — something light on its feet.
strongholds.outro: The lodge is empty. Brask has fled to the great forge — the Iron Maw.

strongholds.name: Anvil Stair
strongholds.intro: The Anvil Stair climbs to the high forges between two ridges of guns. Nobody walks up it in one piece — unless somebody walks up behind them, mending as they go.
strongholds.hint: A long climb under fire is won by whoever stays on his feet the longest. Keep your healers close and out of the guns' first reach.
strongholds.outro: The stair is ours. The monks say they have never prayed so hard in their lives.

strongholds.name: The Iron Maw
strongholds.intro: The Iron Maw: a fortress forge with an outer wall of stone and a Bastion full of Brask's best, ready to march out at the first sight of us.
strongholds.hint: Come near the Bastion and its garrison marches out to meet you. A long fight wants healing close at hand.
strongholds.outro: The Maw is broken. Brask Ironjaw is on the run with nowhere left to hide but his last furnace.

strongholds.name: Furnace Gate
strongholds.intro: At the Furnace Gate, Brask's last fortress before his own forge, the captains asked for you by name. This time, Lord, you ride with us.
strongholds.hint: Your war cry can turn a losing fight around — once. Ride where the fighting is hardest, and choose the moment well.
strongholds.outro: The gate is broken and the men have seen their Lord at the front. Brask's last forge lies ahead.

strongholds.name: Brask's Last Forge
strongholds.intro: Brask Ironjaw's last forge is a castle — real stone, archers on every wall, and Brask himself waiting at his hall with his hammer.
strongholds.hint: Brask fights in person, and he won't stray far from his hall. Choose the ground where you meet him, and the moment for your war cry.
strongholds.outro: Brask laid down his hammer. In his forge we found a map of the sea — and a crow's feather on the Raven King's island.

strongholds.name: Black Sail Cove
strongholds.intro: The Raven fleet lies beached in Black Sail Cove, and the cove's mortars cover every yard of open ground around it.
strongholds.hint: Mortars love a crowd on open ground. Don't give them one — and don't give them time to reload, either.
strongholds.outro: The cove is ours, and the Raven fleet burns on the sand.

strongholds.name: Smuggler's Wharf
strongholds.intro: The smugglers' wharf is piled high with timber and tar — and the paths between the stacks are not as empty as they look.
strongholds.hint: Smugglers hide what they love and guard what they fear. Don't trust the tidy paths between the stacks — and remember what a wharf is made of.
strongholds.outro: The tar went up, the smugglers ran, and the wharf is ours — what is left of it.

strongholds.name: Gallows Reef
strongholds.intro: On Gallows Reef the Ravens hang their prisoners where our ships can see them. The reef looks empty — too empty.
strongholds.hint: Empty ground on a Raven island is never empty. Something should look before the rest of the company walks.
strongholds.outro: The prisoners are free and the ambushers are swimming home.

strongholds.name: Stormbreak Battery
strongholds.intro: Stormbreak's guns stand behind a stone sea wall, and ballistas at either end of the beach watch every approach.
strongholds.hint: Ballista bolts go through every man in a line, and a long beach makes long lines easy. Wherever you cross, be unseen while you do it.
strongholds.outro: The battery is silent. Nothing now stands between our army and the Roost.

strongholds.name: Rookery
strongholds.intro: The Rookery is where Corvane breeds his ravens and keeps his towers thickest. Here the Lady joins the army, her banner at the front of the line.
strongholds.hint: Her banner shields everyone close beneath it — for a while. Raise it where the arrows fall thickest.
strongholds.outro: The ravens scattered over the sea, and the Lady's banner flies over the Rookery.

strongholds.name: Elephant Pass
strongholds.intro: The road to the Roost's causeway runs through a narrow pass, and the Ravens have filled it with guns. The Lady's banner leads the way.
strongholds.hint: Every gun in the pass turns on whatever leads the way. One beast can take a terrible beating, your archers none at all — and a banner covers only those close beneath it.
strongholds.outro: The pass is open. The causeway to the Roost lies ahead.

strongholds.name: Black Feather Hall
strongholds.intro: Black Feather Hall is home to Corvane's champion, the Raven Lady, who waits at her hall with a bow that never misses.
strongholds.hint: She fights at her hall and nowhere else. Make her come to you, and don't let her pick off the soft men while she does.
strongholds.outro: The Raven Lady has yielded her bow. Only Kingsbane and the Roost itself remain.

strongholds.name: Kingsbane Walls
strongholds.intro: The Roost's outer walls — Kingsbane, the Ravens call them, because no king has ever crossed them. Corvane's champions, a lord and a lady, wait at the hall beside the keep.
strongholds.hint: No king has crossed these walls, and the Roost's champions wait at their hall. Choose where they fight you — and who they meet first.
strongholds.outro: Kingsbane has fallen. Let them find a new name for it.

strongholds.name: Corvane's Stair
strongholds.intro: The stair to the Roost is Corvane's last gate: every gun, every engine and every champion he has left, packed into one fortress on the cliff.
strongholds.hint: You have every tool you have ever needed. The Stair will test whether you remember which one each wall, gun and champion fears.
strongholds.outro: The Stair has fallen. Above us, through the sea mist, rise the towers of Ravenhold.

strongholds.name: Ravenhold
strongholds.intro: Ravenhold. The Raven King's castle stands where the land meets the sea, its banners black against the sunrise and its yards hidden in sea mist. Corvane himself waits at his hall. Everything we have done leads here.
strongholds.hint: Everything the Raven King has, he has put here. Everything you've learned, you'll need here. Spend each where it counts.
strongholds.outro: Corvane, the Raven King, has thrown down his crown. The coast is free. Long live the Lord of the Horizon!

strongholds.name: Saltgate Landing
strongholds.intro: The Ashen Legion has come ashore at Saltgate and piled its supplies on our beach: grain, powder, pay chests. Guns and towers stand all round the heaps.
strongholds.hint: An army marches on its stores. Some riders of ours were born to find them — fast enough to get there before the guns turn.
strongholds.outro: Saltgate is ash and the Legion goes hungry. Marshal Varro will have to ship his bread across the whole sea now.

strongholds.name: Ashwall Redoubt
strongholds.intro: The Legion builds the way it marches: in straight lines and three deep. The Ashwall Redoubt is one ring of imperial stone as thick as a house, and its engineers are proud of every block.
strongholds.hint: Stone that took a month to raise can come down in a heartbeat. Don't waste that heartbeat on the wrong stretch of wall.
strongholds.outro: The engineers are still counting the holes in their walls. We left them plenty to count.

strongholds.name: Boltwork Bastion
strongholds.intro: Varro's Boltwork Bastion: guns packed shoulder to shoulder behind one wall, every one of them cast in the imperial foundries.
strongholds.hint: Swords will never reach those guns alive. Bolts that crack stone can — if somebody keeps the arrows off the men who loose them.
strongholds.outro: The Bastion's guns lie split like firewood. The crossbowmen have asked for a day off. They have earned two.

strongholds.name: Remount Plains
strongholds.intro: On the Remount Plains the Legion breaks its horses. Mortars and heavy bows cover miles of open grass — and the grass hides nooses.
strongholds.hint: Big engines are slow to turn, and they love a crowd. Bows spread wide are bows they never quite hit — as long as they watch where they walk.
strongholds.outro: The Legion's horses are ours now. The archers have already given each of them a name.

strongholds.name: Trapper's Keep
strongholds.intro: Varro's trappers hold a castle in the misty woods. Every path to it is dug, spiked, tarred and noosed, and nobody has walked out of those woods in a year.
strongholds.hint: The worst trap is the one you never saw. Light the way before the company walks it — and let the strongest feet go first.
strongholds.outro: We marched out of the trappers' woods, all of us. The trappers are still looking for the way out.

strongholds.name: Smokewater Lines
strongholds.intro: The Smokewater Lines guard the road to the Legion's camp: every gun the Marshal could spare, behind one long wall. Our armoury has sent its best — at full strength.
strongholds.hint: The quartermaster sent smoke, horns and herbs at their strongest. Each of them is worth a dozen men — at the right moment, in the right place.
strongholds.outro: The Lines are broken. Through the smoke, the Legion's great camp is in sight.

strongholds.name: The Imperial Wall
strongholds.intro: The Imperial Wall: everything an imperial Keep may hold — five cannons, five towers, three mortars, three ballistas, a castle — behind more stone than the whole Iron Hills.
strongholds.hint: So many walls and so many guns can't all be fought at once. Pick one quarter, break into it with everything — then the next.
strongholds.outro: The Wall that was meant to stand a thousand years stood until lunch. The Legion is falling back to Ashenhold.

strongholds.name: Ashen Court
strongholds.intro: At the Ashen Court, Varro's Lady Commander holds the hall. She was the best archer of the old empire, and she has never missed.
strongholds.hint: Her bow outreaches every tower on the walls. Bring her down to your champions' level — close, where her arrows are worth less than their blades.
strongholds.outro: The Lady Commander gave up her bow with a bow. Varro has nobody left between us and his own gate.

strongholds.name: Legion Keep
strongholds.intro: Legion Keep, Varro's last fort before Ashenhold. Its champion, the Iron Lord, has fought in a hundred battles and lost none.
strongholds.hint: The Iron Lord is worth an army on his own. Keep your company out of his reach until it can face him together — or keep him busy while the rest does the work.
strongholds.outro: The Iron Lord has lost his first battle. He took it well: he asked to fight beside you.

strongholds.name: Ashenhold
strongholds.intro: Ashenhold, the Marshal's citadel, wrapped in the smoke of its own forges. Varro and his Lady Commander wait in the hall, with every gun an empire can give.
strongholds.hint: Every wall, gun, trap and champion the empire has is here, at its strongest. So is everything you have. Spend it all — and spend it well.
strongholds.outro: Marshal Varro has knelt and handed over his baton. The empire beyond the sea will send envoys, not legions. Long live the Lord of the Horizon — Emperor of the Coast!
